itineraries.title: Miracle on the Malacca - 4 Day Itinerary
editorial: We organised our four days loosely around flora, fauna, terra, and aqua (you’ll see what we mean in a moment).
What if we had more time?

We spent the perfect amount of time in Singapore, especially considering we’ve given similar durations to much larger nations. That said, we skipped Universal Studios as we’ve been to ones in the US, so if that’s on your itinerary, you’ll need another day.

days.title: Day 1 - Flora
editorial: Our trip started with the exploration of Changi airport, often recognised at the best in the world (and we couldn’t agree more). There are multiple gardens inside the airport, including the five-storeyed Forest Valley with the Rain Vortext (the tallest indoor waterfall) as it’s centrepiece.
Once in the city, our first stop were the Gardens by the Bay. Among its attractions is the Flower Dome, the largest glass greenhouse in the world which hosts plants and trees from across the world.
After you’re done admiring natural botany, and the sun starts setting, the futuristic Supertree Grove structures light up.

days.title: Day 2 - Fauna
editorial: Day two is for the zoo. The enclosures are designed to feel natural, for both the human onlookers and the animal residents.

After sauntering through the zoo in the day, we returned at night for the Night Safari. It’s a surreal to see the animals in the dark, with just the right amount of fake moonlight adding to the atmospehre.
One practical advice… food outlets inside the attractions close earlier than the attractions themselves. The main cafe shut around 4:30 PM for instance.

Between fawning over fauna, we hit the Maxwell Food Centre in Chinatown for some sumptuous street food. We noticed that many of the people manning the food stalls were quite elderly, a reminder that Singapore’s economic miracle did not arrive at the same time for every generations.

days.title: Day 3 - Terra
editorial: It was finally time for us to explore the city landscape.
We paid homage at the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple and the Thian Hock Keng Temple (the latter is of the Taoist faith), which are about 500m apart from each other.

We then got out our shopping bags and  explored the neighbourhoods of Orchard Road, Bugis, and Arab Street. Unlike other attractions in Singapore (like the zoo) that are uniquely designed, we found the malls to be just like any other place. Luxury retail looks alike (when you can’t afford it anyway).

days.title: Day 4 - Aqua
editorial: It was back to nature for our last day, with a cable car ride down to Sentosa island for the Singapore Oceanarium (formerly known as the S.E.A Aquarium).
We gave Universal Studios a miss as we’d already been to the ones in California and Florida (in the US).
We returned to the mainland for a tour of the observatory atop Marina Bay Sands. We decided to go at an off-peak time (3:00 PM) to avoid large crowds.
We ended our stay with a stroll along the promenade, where the Merlion stands in all its glory against the backdrop of the historic Raffles Hotel.
